newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit says to dispose of bad loans as planned.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit says to dispose of bad loans as planned.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd said on Wednesday that it will dispose of 130 billion yen worth of problem loans in the 1996/97 fiscal year.
NCB vice president Shoji Nishikawa told reporters that the bank had no liquidity problems and that it would carry out its problem loan disposal as planned.

Referring to the sharp fall in its stock price and debentures, Nishikawa said trading in its shares and debentures was influenced by exaggerated media reports which hyped concerns over the health of Japan's financial system.
"We believe the market condition has deviated greatly from the realities of the bank. We hope market participants will calm down," he said.
NCB said it had called the news conference to deny rumours circulating in the market that the bank was near collapse.
The rumours had pushed up Japanese government bond prices on Wednesday morning and triggered selling of NCB stocks.
NCB's share price fell to its lowest level for the current financial year, closing down 35 yen at 181 yen. The shares' previous 1996/97 low was 210 yen marked on January 29, 1997.
